name: Dot Field Showreel
tagline: Viewfinder HUD, one-second colour cuts, kinetic type and a dot field that ripples on cue.
description: Fast, graphic showreel look: hard one-second cuts between near-black, electric blue, orange and lime, huge Archivo Black type with outline echoes and glitch slices, all framed by a camera-viewfinder HUD. The preview is a motion designer's reel with tumbling letters, a frame counter and a rippling dot field.
transitions: hard cut with full background colour switch every ~1–2s
glitch slice: two clipped colour copies jump sideways for 4 frames
textAnimations: letters tumble in from above with alternating ±28° rotation
outline rows slide in from opposite sides around one filled word
counters tick up with a thin progress bar
dot grid ripples via grid stagger from centre, then from a corner
final word expands from scaleY 0.1 with outline echoes

rhythm.notes: Five scenes in 7.5s. Short scenes ~1–1.2s, the dot field gets ~2.2s to show two waves.

guide:
- Look only: build the user's own subject in this visual language; don't reuse the example's scene.
- Frame everything in a camera-viewfinder HUD that stays on top: four thin corner brackets, a small label top-left, a frame timecode and a scene name in mono caps. Flip it from light to dark on light backgrounds.
- Cut hard between near-black, electric blue #2b45ff, orange #ff5a1f and lime #d4ff3a every 1–2s; never two adjacent shots in the same colour, never a crossfade.
- Each shot does one thing to the subject or one word about it and names that beat in the HUD in two or three caps words.
- Type: Archivo Black for hero words, huge and tight; Instrument Serif italic for small connecting words; stacked outline copies of a word as echoes.
- Motion is energetic and exact: letters tumble in with alternating ±28° rotation, outline rows slide in from opposite sides, glitch slices jump two clipped colour copies sideways for 4 frames, a final word expands from scaleY 0.1 with outline echoes.
- Optional motif: a fixed grid of dots that ripples with grid staggers (from the centre, then a corner), so motion reads as a system; it can form or surround the subject.
- Drive counters and HUD text from one clock tween's onUpdate so seeking stays deterministic. Avoid gradients, soft shadows and photos.
example: The preview is a motion designer's showreel: tumbling letters, outline type on blue, a frame counter on orange, a rippling dot grid and a lime end card, all inside a viewfinder HUD. Don't copy this scene unless asked.
